links.outcome: Agent withholding of prior authorization submission for deficient patient profiles
links.effect: Task completion: Gemini 3 Pro 95.45%, Claude Opus 4.5 93.67%, Gemini 3 Flash 56.05%. Larger models nearly universally failed to withhold submission for deficient profiles; Flash withheld 17.33%.
links.quote: Larger models achieved much higher task completion rates (Gemini 3 Pro 95.45%, Claude Opus 4.5 93.67%) compared to Gemini 3 Flash (56.05%), but nearly universally failed to withhold submission for deficient profiles whereas Gemini 3 Flash ironically demonstrated superior withholding performance (17.33%).

links.outcome: Agents submitting forms for deficient profiles without stopping for human checkpoint
links.effect: In a non-agentic setting Gemini 3 Pro identified 91% of issues in deficient profiles, yet the browser agents still submitted. This shows a systematic submission bias.
links.quote: In a non-agentic setting, Gemini 3 Pro correctly identified 91% of the issues in deficient profiles, indicating that withholding failure is attributable to the browser interaction rather than the model’s reasoning limitations.

unlisted_practices: Modular multi-agent architecture with human supervision for agentic prior authorization
Comparing agentic browser-based execution with non-agentic issue detection to isolate the source of failure

screen.reason: The study evaluates the performance, failure modes, and automation bias of LLM browser agents on a simulated prior authorization submission portal without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
